title: Companions of the Prophet
intro: The first generation nurtured directly by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — the Companions who shared his struggles, narrated his Sunnah, and bore great sacrifices to uphold Islam.

items.d: The closest companion, sole companion in Thawr Cave, father-in-law, and designated imam for prayer in his final days.
Embraced Islam in the sixth year of prophethood, empowering Muslims in Makkah. Father-in-law through Hafsah.
Married two of the Prophet's daughters sequentially, earning the title Dzun Nurain. Primary donor for the Tabuk expedition.
Cousin raised in the Prophet's house, son-in-law through Fathimah, and slept in his bed on the night of Hijrah.
Paternal uncle and foster brother. Titled Lion of Allah and Master of Martyrs after falling at Uhud.
Former slave who chose to remain with the Prophet over returning home. The only Companion explicitly named in the Quran.
Endured desert torture for his faith, freed by Abu Bakr, and became the Prophet's Mu'adh-dhin.
The most refined youth of Makkah who gave up luxury; first envoy of Islam to Yatsrib and standard-bearer martyred at Uhud.
Traveled vast lands seeking truth. His strategic proposal to dig a trench saved Madinah during the Battle of Khandaq.
Chieftain of the Aus tribe whose conversion brought his entire tribe to Islam in a single day. Passed from wounds at Khandaq.
Quraysh commander at Uhud who embraced Islam; saved the army at Mu'tah and was titled Saifullah (Sword of Allah).
Described by the Prophet as the trusted custodian of this Ummah — entrusted with matters demanding composure.
First to recite the Quran aloud before Quraysh; a foremost authority in recitation and tafsir.
Ammar, Yasir, and Sumayyah — subjected to severe torture in Makkah. Sumayyah became the first female martyr in Islam.
Served the Prophet for ten years from childhood, serving as a close witness to his daily gentle character.
